end.summary:
- Sequenced key dates: Charter (1600), Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), and Crown rule (1858).
- Explained the Company’s shift from trading to political control.
- Identified Mir Jafar’s role after Plassey and the combined forces defeated at Buxar.
- Explained Diwani rights (1765) as revenue-collection rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
- Needed more practice explaining the full set of methods used to gain power.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised how the East India Company changed from a trading company into a ruler, using dates, Plassey, Buxar and Diwani rights. They clearly explained the sequence and how revenue collection supported the Company’s trade and army. There was a mix-up about who helped the Company at Plassey; this was corrected later by identifying Mir Jafar and his role. At home, ask Zoya to make a five-step flow chart including forts, armies, alliances, battles and revenue rights.
